one_liner: Single-file AVX2/SSE4 UTF-8 validator in C; about 1.5-1.7x faster than fastvalidate-utf-8 AVX2 on random UTF-8.
what_it_does: Checks whether a byte buffer is well-formed UTF-8 (rejecting overlongs, surrogates, code points above U+10FFFF and bad continuation structure) and returns 1 or 0; it does not locate the error or transcode. The library is one C file, z_validate.c, compiled with -DAVX2 or -DSSE4 to produce z_validate_utf8_avx2 or z_validate_utf8_sse4(const char *data, size_t len). There is no header, so callers declare the prototype themselves. The (pointer, length) shape matches fastvalidate-utf-8's validators, but the function name differs and it returns int instead of bool.
how_it_is_fast: Continuation structure is checked in the scalar domain on movemask bitmasks: masks of bytes starting 11, 111 and 1111 are shifted forward 1, 2 and 3 positions and summed with one lea-style add into a 'required continuation' mask, which must equal the mask of actual 10xxxxxx bytes. A carry mask handles sequences that cross vector boundaries. The special-case errors (C0/C1 and E0/F0 overlongs, ED surrogates, F4 above U+10FFFF, F5-FF) are found with three vpshufb nibble lookups (the high and low nibble of the previous byte and the high nibble of the current byte), ANDed into one error-bit vector that must be zero. This three-nibble-lookup idea was adopted by the Keiser-Lemire 'lookup' algorithm now in simdutf. All-ASCII vectors exit after a single movemask test.
when_to_use: Studying or teaching SIMD UTF-8 validation: the long comment in z_validate.c is one of the clearest write-ups of the nibble-lookup error tables
Vendoring a tiny, dependency-free validator into a C codebase that already targets AVX2 at build time, after fixing the tail over-read described under gotchas
Mostly non-ASCII text (CJK, mixed scripts) on Haswell-or-newer x86, where it measured 0.26-0.29 cycles/byte versus 0.41-0.50 for fastvalidate-utf-8
Buffers from KiB to MiB sizes where only a valid/invalid answer is needed, not the error position
when_not_to_use: Production code: use simdutf, which implements the successor lookup algorithm with runtime CPU dispatch, AVX-512 and NEON kernels, error positions and transcoding, and is maintained
Pure-ASCII workloads: no gain over fastvalidate-utf-8's asciipath variant (0.079 vs 0.074 cycles/byte at 64K, 0.160 vs 0.156 at 16M)
ARM, POWER or other non-x86 targets: master has only AVX2 and SSE4 paths; the AVX-512 and NEON work exists only on an unmerged wip branch whose AVX-512 build fails its own tests (issue #6)
Binaries that must run on unknown x86 CPUs: there is no runtime dispatch, so an AVX2 build raises SIGILL on pre-Haswell parts
Buffers that end near an unmapped page, or code run under ASan or Valgrind, until the tail over-read is fixed

integration.min_toolchain: C99/C11 compiler with x86 intrinsics; the repo's rules.py uses cc -std=gnu11 -O3 -march=native (the -fcolor-diagnostics flag suggests clang); compiler version not documented
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 (-DAVX2) or SSSE3 plus SSE4.1 (-DSSE4, needed for _mm_test_all_zeros); no ARM on master
integration.thread_safety: Reentrant: a pure function with no global or static mutable state (checked in the source); not documented in the README
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same (const char*, size_t) shape as fastvalidate-utf-8's validate_utf8_fast_avx, but a different name, an int return, and a compile-time ISA macro instead of a header

gotchas: Out-of-bounds read: the main loop loads the next shifted vector, v_load(data + offset + V_LEN - 1), before re-testing the loop condition. On the last loop iteration it therefore reads up to 30 bytes (AVX2) or 14 bytes (SSE4) past the end of the input, for every length above one vector except lengths of 0 or V_LEN-1 modulo V_LEN (60 of the 65 lengths from 32 to 96 with AVX2, counted with a Python model of the loop). The value is discarded, so results are unaffected. The read can still fault when the buffer ends near an unmapped page, and ASan will report it. test.lua cannot see it because it embeds every input in a padded 128-byte buffer. Fix: load data + offset - 1 at the top of the next iteration. Codegen was not inspected because nothing was built here.

The validation logic itself checks out: a Python model of HEAD's masks and tables agreed with Python's strict UTF-8 decoder on 4.25 million crafted inputs (all two-byte pairs with continuation and ASCII tails at boundary offsets, plus token fuzzing, for vector widths 32 and 16). The F0-overlong fix (2b0ad07) changed only table constants, and the ASCII early-exit change (cf48201) only affects invalid input, so the README timings still reflect HEAD on valid data.

Build traps: z_validate_vec is declared plain 'inline' (not static). Under C99/C11 inline rules, an unoptimised build has no out-of-line definition; rules.py's avx2/deb and sse4/deb configs use -g with no -O. The 'cont' variable draws a maybe-uninitialised warning that -Werror turns into a build error; the maintainer agreed to fix it in issue #5, but the fix never landed. test.lua declares the functions as returning bool while the C returns int.
Compiler sensitivity: a user reported (issue #5) that a hand-unrolled variant ran about 2x faster under MSVC 2017, so the published cycles/byte assume a GCC/Clang-style compiler (unstated).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against lemire/validateutf8-experiments (the lookup algorithm, labelled research-only): this is the smaller, self-contained C file, and the same lookup idea in production form is simdutf, which should be preferred for shipped code. Pick zwegner's file only when you want a dependency-free single source file to read or vendor on AVX2-only x86.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README, best of 50 runs on a 2.4 GHz Haswell laptop with a private modification of the fastvalidate-utf-8 harness (compiler unstated): AVX2 validates random UTF-8 at 0.264 cycles/byte (64K) and 0.290 (16M), against 0.410/0.436 and 0.496/0.457 for fastvalidate-utf-8's two AVX2 functions (about 1.55-1.71x, derived), with no gain on pure ASCII. Lemire's validateutf8-experiments README (an adapted port named zwegneravx, CMake Release with -march=native, unnamed 3.5 GHz CPU) independently shows 19.7 GB/s on hongkong.html and 41.0 GB/s on twitter.json. That is 1.28x and 1.82x the fastvalidate-style 'basic' row (15.5 and 22.5 GB/s), and 0.94x and 1.11x the lookup4 algorithm (20.9 and 37.0 GB/s) (ratios derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-11-18 (9 commits; the maintainer's 2020 wip branch with AVX-512/NEON never reached master). MIT-licensed via the z_validate.c header only, with no LICENSE file. It is small enough to vendor, but fix the tail over-read first; for production prefer simdutf.
